QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_45

answer.text: Identifying suspicious transactions, maintaining records, and reporting unusual activities

explanation.text: The Logic: AML/CFT obligations under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act and related rules require reporting entities — including AIFs and their service providers — to identify and monitor suspicious transactions, maintain prescribed transaction and identification records, and report unusual or suspicious activities to the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU-IND) through Suspicious Transaction Reports. AML is not limited to large investigations, not limited to bank-account checks, and applies to securities-market intermediaries and AIFs, not only to banks. The Trap: "AML applies only to banks" is a common misconception — PMLA reporting obligations extend across financial intermediaries, including AIFs and their distributors. Note: A direct enumeration of "identifying suspicious transactions, maintaining records, and reporting unusual activities" as AML obligations is not present in the NISM Series XIX-A AIF (Category I and II) Distributors workbook pages checked; the framing here reflects general PMLA/AML obligations under Indian regulation rather than a workbook citation.
